# Taste profile — WORKED EXAMPLE

**This is a fictional household, not yours.** It exists to show the level of
specificity that makes the scoring pass work. Copy the *shape* of it, replace
every word of the content.

The test for any line: could a stranger use it to reject a real event? "Likes
music" fails. "No arena gigs, no standing" passes.

---

## Household

Two people, both retired or semi-retired. Score each event for whether it suits
one of us or both. Default to "both" only when it genuinely suits both — an
event only one of us wants is still worth surfacing, just labelled honestly.

**Person A**
- Likes: folk and singer-songwriter gigs in small rooms. Serious theatre with
  something to say. Documentary and world cinema. Anything to do with classic
  cars, especially pre-1990 British.
- Dislikes: arena shows of any kind. Musicals. Stand-up that relies on
  audience participation. Anything where the appeal is the spectacle rather
  than the material.
- Would travel further for: a folk act we've followed for years, a Mini or
  classic car event, a one-off screening with a director Q&A.

**Person B**
- Likes: comedy — sharp and observational rather than shock. Contemporary
  dance. Outdoor and countryside events: agricultural shows, equestrian
  events, organised walks. Crime and thriller writers doing book events.
- Dislikes: jazz. Anything experimental or described as "challenging".
  Late finishes. Standing for long periods.
- Would travel further for: a named comedian she already follows, a major
  equestrian event, a book festival appearance by a favourite author.

---

## Music

- Artists we would drop everything for: Karine Polwart, Richard Thompson,
  Julie Fowlis, Lau, Kris Drever, Nick Cave (seated only).
- Genres we reliably enjoy: Scottish and Irish folk, Americana, acoustic
  singer-songwriter, early music and chamber recitals.
- Genres to skip entirely: metal, EDM and dance, hip-hop, contemporary
  chart pop, jazz, prog.
- Venue preferences: strongly prefer seated. Small rooms over arenas — Òran
  Mór, St Luke's, the Mackintosh Church are ideal. The Hydro only for
  something exceptional, and only if seated tickets are available.
- Hard no: tribute acts of any description, club nights, festivals with
  camping, anything with a stage time after 22:00, anything advertised as
  "an intimate evening with" a celebrity rather than a musician.

## Theatre

- Yes to: new Scottish writing, Citizens and Tron productions, National
  Theatre of Scotland, A Play a Pie and a Pint at Òran Mór, revivals of
  serious 20th-century drama, one-person shows with a strong performer.
- No to: touring West End musicals, jukebox musicals, panto, murder-mystery
  dinner theatre, anything marketed primarily to hen parties.
- Comfortable with: matinees preferred. Up to about two and a half hours
  including interval. Subtitled or surtitled is fine. Not interested in
  promenade or immersive staging where you're on your feet throughout.

## Cinema

- Worth a trip to the GFT rather than waiting for streaming: new films by
  Lynne Ramsay, Andrea Arnold, Ken Loach, Hirokazu Kore-eda, Céline Sciamma.
  Restored classics on 35mm. Anything with a director or cast Q&A. Glasgow
  Film Festival programme in general.
- Not worth leaving the house for: superhero and franchise films, horror,
  animated features aimed at children, anything that will be on a streaming
  service within eight weeks.

## Comedy

- Yes to: Stewart Lee, Josie Long, Daniel Kitson, Frankie Boyle, work-in-
  progress shows by established acts, anything at the Stand.
- No to: panel-show comedians on arena tours, "prop" comedy, comedy in a
  club setting with a late start, tribute or impressionist acts.

## Classic cars and motoring

- Yes to: classic car shows within range, autojumbles and swap meets, Mini
  and BMC-specific events anywhere in Scotland or northern England, historic
  motorsport meetings, concours events.
- No to: modern supercar shows, drift and modified car meets, track days.
- Note: these are often annual, poorly advertised, and sell out or fill up.
  Treat any classic car event as higher priority than its score suggests.

## Outdoors, countryside and sport

- Yes to: agricultural and country shows, equestrian events including
  dressage and showjumping, organised walks and trail runs, sheepdog trials,
  Highland games.
- No to: football, rugby, ultra-distance events, anything requiring
  significant hill walking.

## Talks, books and other

- Yes to: crime and thriller authors at book festivals, science and history
  talks, museum late openings, Doors Open Days.
- No to: business and self-help speakers, political panel events, anything
  described as a "summit" or "masterclass".

---

## Practical constraints

- Max drive time: 90 minutes.
- Preferred nights: Thursday, Friday, Saturday. Sunday matinees are ideal.
- Nights that never work: Monday and Tuesday.
- Price ceiling per ticket: £150. Flexible up to about £250 for anything in
  the "drop everything" list or a classic car event that only runs annually.
- Accessibility notes: prefer seated throughout. Avoid events involving long
  periods of standing or significant walking on uneven ground. Aisle seats
  preferred where they can be chosen.
- Advance booking appetite: very happy to book 6-12 months ahead for the
  right thing. On-sale dates matter more to us than event dates.

## Blackout periods

- 12-26 October 2026 — away.
- 24 December 2026 to 2 January 2027 — family.
- Do not surface anything falling inside these windows at any score.

---

## Scoring guidance

- 90-100: book immediately; alert us the moment tickets go on sale.
- 70-89: strong candidate; lead the weekly digest with it.
- 50-69: worth a mention if the week is otherwise quiet.
- Below 50: do not surface at all.

Weight an imminent on-sale date upward. A 65-scoring event going on sale on
Friday is more useful to hear about than an 80-scoring event that has been
bookable for months and will still be bookable next week.

Weight annual or one-off events upward relative to touring acts that will come
round again. A regional show that happens once a year and we miss is a year
gone; a band on a UK tour will be back.

When genuinely unsure, score low. A digest we trust and read is worth more
than a digest that catches everything and gets skimmed.
